problem: Embodied memory work and benchmarks mostly test recall or performance when past experience matches the current episode, and none controls the relation between stored trajectories and the tested episode (start pose, route validity, amount/relevance of history).
motivation: A robot working repeatedly in one warehouse must reuse experience from a new start, around blocked aisles, and among histories collected for other goals. Success on replaying the original conditions does not reveal how well a memory representation transfers, so the paper compares six representations under one frozen policy while varying one kind of mismatch at a time.
key_idea: MemTransfer is a controlled Isaac Sim warehouse benchmark (100 cases, 10 task types, expert demos) that compares six memory representations under a shared frozen VLM policy while varying start pose, route availability, and the amount and relevance of history.
insight: Robustness to one mismatch does not imply robustness to another. Full-context and Episodic memory are near-perfect at the demo start (95.3/100.0 SR) but lose 48-49 points at a new start. Summary is stable across starts but retains only 0.39 of its SR after blocking, less than Working memory (0.45) and the trajectory memories (0.56-0.58). Only Episodic gains from more relevant demos (+14.3 SR), and the replacement experiments show that the composition of the history set matters even at fixed size. The action-vs-image ablation (100% with actions vs 49.0% with images alone) shows the expert-action guidance drives Episodic's matched-condition success.
method: Benchmark environment: an Isaac Sim 4.5 warehouse of about 16x30 m on a 1 m grid with 4 headings; 100 cases (10 task types x 10) covering basic search, multi-object search and loops; no map or object list is given.

Demonstration set: 4 near-optimal planner demos per case (original start, opposite heading, nearby start, distant start), plus a new-start test episode and a blocked-route copy; the test references are excluded from memory construction.

Six representations: Working memory (last h=6 steps), Full-context (actions plus up to 40 keyframes), Summary (sequential summary document), Semantic (consolidated general knowledge), Hybrid (Summary+Semantic concatenated), Episodic (ViT-B/16 view matching that retrieves an expert continuation of 6 actions and views).

Shared policy: a frozen InternVL-style VLM (\vlm{}, bai2026intern) at temperature 0 with a 30-token answer budget, T_max=200 and at most 50 images per prompt; memory is split into a construction step B_r and an access step A_r.

Three comparisons: RQ1 varies the test start or the start of the demo used for memory; RQ2 blocks a shared passage while keeping an alternative route; RQ3 compares 1 vs 4 demos, and replaces 2 of 4 with irrelevant or confusable other-task histories.

Metrics: SR, SPL, baseline-relative change Δ, retention (blocked SR / unchanged SR), follow rate (episodes that tried a blocked cell) and recovery rate (success among those), plus images and tokens per request.

setting.backbone: Frozen VLM policy (name hidden behind a macro; cited as bai2026intern), with a ViT-B/16 encoder for Episodic retrieval
setting.training_data: none (training-free; memories are built from 4 expert demonstrations per case, 400 demos in total, and 600 reference trajectories in total including test references)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (camera 1.2 m high, 90° FOV) + absolute position and heading + action feedback
setting.action_space: discrete grid moves: forward/backward/left/right by 1 cell without changing heading, and turn left/right/around
setting.privileged: none at test time for the policy (absolute pose is given); expert demos come from a planner on the ground-truth map

numbers.evidence: Table 1 (Memory performance across the three RQs), New/Unchanged/4 demos column

numbers.extra: replay reference, test starts at the demo pose; 5 runs

numbers_note: These are the benchmark's own baseline rows: the paper proposes no new method, so numbers are for the evaluated memory representations. Working memory: 22.3 SR / 0.051 SPL at the new start. RQ3 mixed-history results appear only in a figure, not in the text.
results: Episodic memory is best in nearly every condition (100.0 SR at the original start, 51.7 at a new start, 66.0 with 4 demos, 37.0 when blocked), but it drops about 48 points at a new start. Summary is stable across starts (43.0 vs 44.3) but retains only 0.39 after blocking. Full-context has the best recovery rate, 30.5, alongside Episodic's 29.6, versus 11.8 for Working memory.
limitations: Only one frozen VLM backbone, a single warehouse scene and navigation tasks, so generalization to other settings is untested.

Memories are fixed during execution (no updating or forgetting); Hybrid was not evaluated in the 4-demo and blocked settings; replacement in RQ3 confounds interference with the loss of relevant history.
Map-based memories are excluded; the pose is given, and the results show that Episodic's advantage depends on the original-start alignment of demos.
